valuation_philosophy: SoFi Technologies is a national bank holding company (SoFi Bank, N.A.). Reported operating cash flow is dominated by loan originations, loan sales, and deposit flows (FY2025 OCF -$3,742M, FY2023 -$7,227M) and is NOT a meaningful measure of owner earnings for a depository institution -- a conventional unlevered FCF DCF would be mechanically invalid here (it would show the company perpetually burning cash even while it earns a genuine profit). This model instead values SOFI's EQUITY DIRECTLY using a discounted-earnings (residual/distributable-earnings-style) approach on GAAP net income: project net income from a decelerating revenue-growth path times an expanding net-margin path, discount at COST OF EQUITY (not a debt-inclusive WACC -- deposits of $37.5B+ and the $1.8B of bank-supporting debt are operating funding for a bank, not financing leverage to net against enterprise value), and terminate with a Gordon-growth value on Year-5 EPS capped by an exit P/E multiple. net_debt is set to 0 throughout: deposits/corporate debt are not subtracted from equity value. Stock-based compensation ($262M FY2025 on $481M GAAP net income, with zero share buybacks) is charged exactly once, via share-count dilution (2.75%/yr, covering both SBC-driven grants and the ongoing exchange of the $1.1B 0% convertible notes due Oct-2026, which pushed diluted shares from ~1,252M FY2025 to ~1,378M Q1 2026) -- SBC is NOT separately deducted from projected net income, since that would double-charge the same cost. The base year is TTM net income through Q2 2026 (~$636.7M = FY2025 $481.3M - H1'25 $168.4M + Q1'26 $166.7M + Q2'26 $157M), which excludes the one-time tax valuation-allowance release that inflated FY2024's $498.7M GAAP net income, making it a cleaner run-rate anchor than either FY2024 or FY2025 alone.

inputs.shares_outstanding_note: Q1 2026 diluted weighted-average share count, used as the base for projections since it matches the earnings denominator; period-end count was ~1,281M. Diluted count is rising fast (from ~1,252M FY2025 wavg) due to ongoing exchange of the $1.1B 0% convertible notes due Oct-2026 into equity, on top of ordinary SBC dilution.
inputs.net_debt_note: SoFi is a bank holding company. Deposits ($37.5B+) and corporate/bank debt (~$1.8B FY2025) fund the loan book and are operating liabilities, not financing debt to net against enterprise value. Equity is valued directly from discounted earnings; no net-debt adjustment is applied.
inputs.base_year_note: TTM through Q2 2026 = FY2025 NI $481.32M - H1'25 NI $168.38M + Q1'26 NI $166.73M + Q2'26 NI ~$157M = $636.67M. TTM revenue = FY2025 $3,613.35M - H1'25 $1,626.70M + Q1'26 $1,100.37M + Q2'26 ~$1,196.92M (Q2'26 rev estimated from Analysis.json's disclosed +40% YoY vs Q2'25 $854.94M) = $4,283.94M. FY2024 GAAP net income ($498.7M) is excluded as the anchor because it included a one-time tax valuation-allowance benefit; TTM is the cleaner run-rate base.
inputs.sbc_treatment: SBC is not deducted a second time from projected net income (GAAP net income already reflects the SBC expense). Its dilutive cost is charged via the annual_share_growth_pct applied to the share count -- charged exactly once, not twice.
inputs.annual_share_growth_note: Combines ongoing SBC-driven share issuance with continued exchange/conversion of the $1.1B 0% convertible notes due October 2026 (diluted shares rose ~10% in a single quarter, Q4'25 to Q1'26, on convertible conversions alone). 2.75%/yr is a mid-point assumption for the 5-year projection once convertible-driven dilution normalizes.

historical_growth.fcf_note: Not applicable/meaningful -- SoFi is a deposit-funded bank; reported operating cash flow is dominated by loan origination/sale volume and deposit flows, not owner earnings (FY2025 OCF -$3,742M despite $481M of GAAP net income). Discounted GAAP earnings used instead (see valuation_philosophy).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_growth_path (decelerating: 30% -> 25% -> 20% -> 16% -> 13% base case), not a single historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue 3yr CAGR (31.9%) and 5yr CAGR (44.9%) both reflect hypergrowth off a small post-SPAC base and diverge sharply from EPS/net-income growth, which only turned positive in FY2024 and was essentially flat FY2024->FY2025 (-3.5%, due to FY2024's one-time tax benefit). Equity CAGR (~24-26%) is inflated by capital raises (SPAC merger 2021, ATM issuance) as well as retained earnings, not purely organic compounding. None of these historical CAGRs is used directly as the DCF growth driver; the projection instead decelerates from TTM/guided growth (~30-43% YoY across recent quarters) toward a mature ~13% by Year 5, per component build in `assumptions`.

base.rationale: Revenue growth decelerates from TTM run-rate (~35-43% YoY in recent quarters, guided 32-35% for FY2026) toward a mature ~13% by Year 5, broadly consistent with continued member/product growth (35% YoY members, 42% YoY products in Q2 2026) fading as the base scales. Net margin ramps from the TTM 14.9% toward 22% by Year 5, below management's ~25% adjusted-net-income-margin aspiration (FY2026 guide: ~$825M adj NI on ~$4.8B adj revenue = ~17% adj margin) to stay conservative on a GAAP basis, reflecting continued mix-shift toward capital-light fee revenue (Loan Platform Business, Technology Platform, interchange) and operating leverage on the bank charter's lower-cost deposit funding.

bull.rationale: Sustained hyper-growth in members/products drives revenue growth staying near recent actuals for longer; capital-light Loan Platform Business, Technology Platform (Galileo/Technisys), and new crypto/stablecoin (SoFiUSD) revenue lines scale faster and carry higher incremental margins, pushing net margin to 25% by Year 5 -- roughly in line with management's own adjusted-net-income targets on a GAAP basis. Lower cost of equity (11%) reflects reduced execution/credit risk if the capital-light mix shift succeeds as planned.

bear.rationale: A consumer credit downturn or intensifying competition (Chime, Nubank, incumbent banks) slows member growth and personal-loan originations sharply; margin expansion stalls as elevated charge-offs and continued high deposit-rate competition pressure NIM, and convertible-note/SBC dilution continues unabated. Higher cost of equity (13%) reflects SoFi's credit-cycle sensitivity on unsecured personal loans and its still-young, unproven bank credit book.

base.implied_exit_multiple_note: Implied exit P/E on Year-5 EPS; current TTM GAAP P/E is ~36-39x (market cap $23.1-24.8B / TTM NI $636.7M depending on share count basis), so this base case implies substantial multiple contraction, not expansion -- conservative by construction.

entry_price.methodology: Entry = (sum of base-scenario EPS Y1-Y5 discounted at 15% + terminal value per share (computed at cost of equity, the fair exit price a buyer pays in Year 5) discounted at 15% - net_debt) / Year-5 projected shares. net_debt = 0 for this bank equity model (see valuation_philosophy).

sensitivity.note: Base-case scenario structure (revenue growth path, margin path, exit P/E cap of 20x) held fixed; cost of equity and terminal growth varied.

probability_weighted.note: Standard 25/50/25 weighting. Bear case (credit-cycle deterioration on the unsecured personal-loan book, competitive pressure, continued dilution) is weighted equally with bull given SoFi's still-young/unproven bank credit book and high sensitivity to the consumer credit cycle flagged as a 'high' severity risk in the qualitative analysis.

implied_multiples.pe_basis: base IV $12.76 / (TTM NI $636.67M / period-end shares 1,281.4M = $0.497 EPS)
implied_multiples.pb_basis: base IV $12.76 / Q1 2026 BVPS $8.44 (equity $10,811.6M / period-end shares 1,281.4M)
implied_multiples.ps_basis: base IV $12.76 / (TTM revenue $4,283.94M / period-end shares 1,281.4M = $3.34 rev/share)
implied_multiples.ev_ebitda_note: Not meaningful for a deposit-funded bank

current_actual_multiples.pe_ttm_note: Current price $18.03 x period-end shares 1,281.4M / TTM NI $636.67M; using Q1'26 diluted weighted-avg shares (1,378M) instead gives ~39.0x

historical_averages_ex_outliers.pe_note: Only FY2024 (34.0x) and FY2025 (68.1x) are meaningful -- FY2019-2023 all had GAAP losses. FY2021-2022 (SPAC-listing era, stock fell from ~$22 IPO reference to a $4.61 FY2022 close) are noted as bubble/de-rating outliers and excluded from the P/E average by construction (no positive EPS in those years to compute one).
historical_averages_ex_outliers.ps_note: FY2021 P/S of 8.46x reflects SPAC-era euphoria on a pre-bank-charter revenue base and is treated as an outlier, not part of the average.

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Implied P/E on base IV (25.7x) is well below both the two-year average of the only profitable historical years (51.0x) and the current actual TTM P/E (36-39x depending on share count basis) -- the model implies substantial multiple CONTRACTION, not expansion. Implied P/B (1.51x) is below the FY2023-2025 average (2.51x) and max (3.12x). Implied P/S (3.82x) is below the FY2023-2025 average (6.61x). Because base-case upside is negative (-29.2%), the 'price in upper half of historical range with positive upside' trip condition is moot. Caveat: only 2 of 5 post-SPAC fiscal years (FY2024-2025) are GAAP-profitable, so the historical P/E sample is thin and itself includes one very rich year (FY2025 68.1x, arguably part of the current AI/fintech re-rating rather than a stable steady-state multiple) -- judgment applied to lean on the lower FY2024 print (34.0x) and the Gordon-growth-implied exit multiples (9.3x-12.1x across scenarios) as the more conservative anchors, consistent with the earnings-based, non-FCF methodology mandated for a bank holding company.
